name: Subependymal Giant Cell Astrocytoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Tuberous Sclerosis Complex Diagnostic Criteria (2012) - SEGA component

criteria.description: Presence of a subependymal lesion >1 cm in diameter near the foramen of Monro on neuroimaging
Histopathological confirmation of astrocytic tumor with giant cell features
Association with tuberous sclerosis complex clinical features or genetic confirmation of TSC1/TSC2 mutation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Identification of a subependymal lesion >1 cm near the foramen of Monro on imaging, with or without histopathological confirmation and/or TSC diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: SEGA is considered a major diagnostic feature of tuberous sclerosis complex.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Obstructive hydrocephalus due to foramen of Monro obstruction
searchTerms: fluid buildup in brain causing blockage
hydrocephalus from foramen of Monro obstruction

pathognomonic.symptomName: Seizures secondary to tumor mass effect

common.symptomName: Visual disturbances due to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: blurred vision due to intracranial pressure

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting related to intracranial hypertension
searchTerms: nausea caused by increased head pressure
unusual changes in behavior or mood

occasional.symptomName: Hemiparesis due to local mass effect

rare.symptomName: Endocrine abnormalities secondary to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: endocrine dysfunction due to brain involvement

rare.symptomName: Sudden neurological deterioration due to acute hydrocephalus

laboratory: No specific laboratory biomarkers; supportive testing for tuberous sclerosis complex mutations (TSC1/TSC2 gene analysis)
imaging: MRI showing enhancing subependymal mass near foramen of Monro
CT scan may show calcified subependymal nodules
Hydrocephalus on imaging due to obstruction
genetic: Pathogenic variants in TSC1 or TSC2 genes associated with tuberous sclerosis complex
other: Histopathology revealing large gemistocytic astrocytes with giant cell morphology

distinguishingFeatures: Lack of mass effect or hydrocephalus
Typically arises from ependymal lining, not subependymal region
May present with different imaging characteristics

redFlags: Rapid onset of severe headache and vomiting
Signs of acute hydrocephalus such as sudden neurological decline
New onset seizures in a patient with known tuberous sclerosis complex
references: Northrup H, Krueger DA. Tuberous sclerosis complex diagnostic criteria update: recommendations of the 2012 International Tuberous Sclerosis Complex Consensus Conference. Pediatr Neurol. 2013 Oct;49(4):243-54.
Jozwiak S, et al. Subependymal giant cell astrocytoma in tuberous sclerosis complex: clinical features and treatment. J Child Neurol. 2006;21(8):693-700.
Crino PB, Nathanson KL, Henske EP. The tuberous sclerosis complex. N Engl J Med. 2006;355(13):1345-56.
